research.snippet: Research on sycophancy asks whether large language models (LLMs) bend towards what their users want to hear. research.snippet: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming. research.snippet: Online Policy Distillation (OPD) often outperforms offline methods such as Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) by training on trajectories sampled directly from the student. research.title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability
research.snippet: Understanding catastrophic forgetting, in which learning new tasks degrades performance on previously learned tasks, remains a fundamental challenge in continual learning (CL). Existing theoretical analyses often rely on specific model or task structures and offer limited insight into how iterative optimization affects forgetting. research.title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
research.snippet: Agentic reinforcement learning rewards a complete episode, yet the policy needs credit for every decision inside it. Counterfactual branching estimates this credit by re-running the episode after an alternative decision, but the branch draws its sampling noise independently of the factual episode, so the outcome difference mixes the effect of the decision with the luck of everything that follows.
